title: How One Mark Finds Its Reader

scenes.tts: A receptor writes phosphotyrosine marks across its tail. How can one protein find the right mark among all the others?
scenes.caption: A receptor writes phosphotyrosine marks across its tail. How can one protein find the right mark among all the others?
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for both films: proteins and receptor outlines blue; phosphates gold; binding domains teal; matching motif residues green; failed contacts red. Fill the frame with one blue receptor tail carrying several gold phosphate badges. A teal reader drifts between them while a large question mark follows it. Mark every shape schematic. Keep the tail gently flexing.
scenes.narration: A receptor writes phosphotyrosine marks across its tail. How can one protein find the right mark among all the others?

scenes.visual: The moving receptor tail remains behind a brief title: How One Mark Finds Its Reader. Fade the title without clearing the tail.

scenes.tts: Phosphate changes a small surface patch, but the mark usually does little alone. It becomes useful when a reader binds there. The reader brings its host protein into the growing signaling complex. A kinase writes the mark, and a phosphatase can erase it.
scenes.caption: Phosphate changes a small surface patch, but the mark usually does little alone. It becomes useful when a reader binds there. The reader brings its host protein into the growing signaling complex. A kinase writes the mark, and a phosphatase can erase it.
scenes.visual: Zoom onto one gold badge. Nothing else changes until the teal reader settles. Then a large blue host block attached to the reader slides beside the receptor. Label the contact connection, not reaction.
scenes.narration: Phosphate changes a small surface patch, but the mark usually does little alone. It becomes useful when a reader binds there. The reader brings its host protein into the growing signaling complex. A kinase writes the mark, and a phosphatase can erase it.

scenes.tts: An S H two domain is one such reader. Its first binding pocket fits phosphotyrosine. Positively charged side chains help grip the phosphate. Unmodified tyrosine lacks that phosphate, so the pocket cannot make the same contact.
scenes.caption: An SH2 domain is one such reader. Its first binding pocket fits phosphotyrosine. Positively charged side chains help grip the phosphate. Unmodified tyrosine lacks that phosphate, so the pocket cannot make the same contact.
scenes.visual: Transform the teal reader into a large two-part schematic clamp labelled SH2. Its round pocket closes around a gold phosphotyrosine badge. Beside it, an unmodified tyrosine badge tries the pocket and slides away in red.
scenes.narration: An SH2 domain is one such reader. Its first binding pocket fits phosphotyrosine. Positively charged side chains help grip the phosphate. Unmodified tyrosine lacks that phosphate, so the pocket cannot make the same contact.

scenes.tts: That first pocket answers whether tyrosine is phosphorylated. It cannot identify which phosphorylated site this is. A neighboring surface reads residues beside the phosphotyrosine and supplies another layer of preference. Different S H two domains carry differently shaped neighboring surfaces.
scenes.caption: That first pocket answers whether tyrosine is phosphorylated. It cannot identify which phosphorylated site this is. A neighbouring surface reads residues beside the phosphotyrosine and supplies another layer of preference. Different SH2 domains carry differently shaped neighbouring surfaces.
scenes.visual: Keep the phosphate pocket closed. Extend a shallow side groove from the same teal domain. A short row of green residue blocks beside the gold badge settles into that groove. Other phosphorylated sites wait nearby.
scenes.narration: That first pocket answers whether tyrosine is phosphorylated. It cannot identify which phosphorylated site this is. A neighbouring surface reads residues beside the phosphotyrosine and supplies another layer of preference. Different SH2 domains carry differently shaped neighbouring surfaces.

scenes.tts: Now the reader tests both features together. Several tails offer the same gold phosphate. Their neighboring patterns differ. Matching blocks settle into the groove; poor fits make the reader release. Sark-family readers favor one pattern, while other readers favor others.
scenes.caption: Now the reader tests both features together. Several tails offer the same gold phosphate. Their neighbouring patterns differ. Matching blocks settle into the groove; poor fits make the reader release. Src-family readers favour one pattern, while other readers favour others.
scenes.visual: Slide three schematic tails through the fixed SH2 clamp. Each gold badge fits the round pocket. One green neighboring pattern fits the groove; two mismatching patterns flash red and drift free. Never label a site rejected or impossible.
scenes.narration: Now the reader tests both features together. Several tails offer the same gold phosphate. Their neighbouring patterns differ. Matching blocks settle into the groove; poor fits make the reader release. Src-family readers favour one pattern, while other readers favour others.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. Reusable binding domains turn recognized motifs or lipids into protein connections. For S H two, phosphorylation enables the contact, while sequence context helps choose among possible partners. The domain binds; it does not catalyze a reaction.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule. Reusable binding domains turn recognized motifs or lipids into protein connections. For SH2, phosphorylation enables the contact, while sequence context helps choose among possible partners. The domain binds; it does not catalyse a reaction.
scenes.visual: The fitting tail and SH2 host enlarge to fill the frame. Transform their contact into a thick green connection line. Place the rule above it, then keep the connection pulsing slowly.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. Reusable binding domains turn recognized motifs or lipids into protein connections. For SH2, phosphorylation enables the contact, while sequence context helps choose among possible partners. The domain binds; it does not catalyse a reaction.

scenes.tts: Predict before the reader moves. Both tails carry phosphotyrosine. Only the lower neighboring pattern fits this reader's groove. Which tail will retain the reader longer? Watch both parts of the binding surface.
scenes.caption: Predict before the reader moves. Both tails carry phosphotyrosine. Only the lower neighbouring pattern fits this reader's groove. Which tail will retain the reader longer? Watch both parts of the binding surface.
scenes.visual: Show two large tails, each with one gold badge. The upper tail has red neighboring blocks; the lower tail has green fitting blocks. Hold the teal reader exactly between them. Display Which tail retains the reader longer?
scenes.narration: Predict before the reader moves. Both tails carry phosphotyrosine. Only the lower neighbouring pattern fits this reader's groove. Which tail will retain the reader longer? Watch both parts of the binding surface.

scenes.visual: Keep the prediction layout unchanged for the full pause. The two tails flex gently and the teal reader rocks in place without approaching either answer.

scenes.tts: The lower tail makes both contacts, so it retains this reader more strongly in this comparison. The upper tail still has phosphate. Its neighboring pattern simply provides a poorer fit for this domain. Another S H two domain could prefer a different pattern.
scenes.caption: The lower tail makes both contacts, so it retains this reader more strongly in this comparison. The upper tail still has phosphate. Its neighbouring pattern simply provides a poorer fit for this domain. Another SH2 domain could prefer a different pattern.
scenes.visual: Move the reader to the lower tail. Close its phosphate pocket, then settle the green pattern into the groove. Let the upper tail remain visible and phosphorylated, labelled poorer fit rather than rejected.
scenes.narration: The lower tail makes both contacts, so it retains this reader more strongly in this comparison. The upper tail still has phosphate. Its neighbouring pattern simply provides a poorer fit for this domain. Another SH2 domain could prefer a different pattern.

scenes.tts: The domain is modular because it keeps this binding activity when moved. Detach the reader from one host. Attach it to a different host, and its preferred target remains the same. The new host can bring a different cellular activity to that site.
scenes.caption: The domain is modular because it keeps this binding activity when moved. Detach the reader from one host. Attach it to a different host, and its preferred target remains the same. The new host can bring a different cellular activity to that site.
scenes.visual: Detach the intact teal SH2 clamp from a blue enzyme block. Move it across the frame and snap it onto a differently shaped blue scaffold block. The same green-and-gold target reconnects to it.
scenes.narration: The domain is modular because it keeps this binding activity when moved. Detach the reader from one host. Attach it to a different host, and its preferred target remains the same. The new host can bring a different cellular activity to that site.

scenes.tts: Preference is not destiny. Location, abundance, timing, and the rest of the host protein also shape contacts in cells. The domain narrows the candidates; cellular context narrows them further. A preferred motif cannot recruit a reader that never reaches it.
scenes.caption: Preference is not destiny. Location, abundance, timing, and the rest of the host protein also shape contacts in cells. The domain narrows the candidates; cellular context narrows them further. A preferred motif cannot recruit a reader that never reaches it.
scenes.visual: Keep the transplanted reader centered. Surround it with four moving filters labelled location, abundance, timing, and host context. Several possible blue partners pass through; more than one remains possible. Label the layout schematic.
scenes.narration: Preference is not destiny. Location, abundance, timing, and the rest of the host protein also shape contacts in cells. The domain narrows the candidates; cellular context narrows them further. A preferred motif cannot recruit a reader that never reaches it.

scenes.tts: Other modules apply the same logic to other targets. S H three reads proline-rich motifs, while some P H domains read membrane lipids. The target changes, but recognition still creates a connection. For P H, that connection is to the membrane.
scenes.caption: Other modules apply the same logic to other targets. SH3 reads proline-rich motifs, while some PH domains read membrane lipids. The target changes, but recognition still creates a connection. For PH, that connection is to the membrane.
scenes.visual: Transform the teal SH2 clamp into a labelled SH3 groove gripping a green motif. Then transform it into a labelled PH pocket touching one green lipid head in a membrane bar. Keep all pictures schematic and retain the same colour map.
scenes.narration: Other modules apply the same logic to other targets. SH3 reads proline-rich motifs, while some PH domains read membrane lipids. The target changes, but recognition still creates a connection. For PH, that connection is to the membrane.

scenes.visual: One-line end card only, centered in large type: 'Reusable binding domains turn recognized motifs or lipids into protein connections.' No subtitle, logo, teaser, or second line.
